answer: Each identity locks a 60 bond in the ivory ledger and pays a 20 auditor fee on filing. After filing, the orchard pool assigns one auditor at random; that auditor stakes 30 and must co-sign with a velvet seal before payment releases. A fake identity pays 80 and risks 60, so the 1000th fake pays 80 and 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 plus 20,000 in fees. An honest identity pays 20 once and recovers 60 after approval. A rented-auditor ring fails because assignment follows filing and cannot be chosen, and an auditor approving bad work loses 30. Anyone can recheck the ledger and seal.
